text:
devon: heads up — after yesterday's autotuner change i'm seeing a perf regression on long tail seqlens when torch.compile + cudagraphs are enabled. latency SLOs violated on a couple steady-state pods.
anna: hmm, ok. any repro or profile snippets?
devon: minimal repro attached in prod-ci job 41 (stack trace + perf). here's the important bit from the perftop: 
```
seqlen=32  p50=16ms  p95=28ms  kernel_group=fast_kv_v2  kernel_hash=ab12ff
seqlen=512 p50=41ms  p95=120ms kernel_group=slow_attn   kernel_hash=ab12ff
```
Note the same kernel_hash for different kernel_group picks. that looks wrong.
mike: same kernel_hash for different code paths -> sounds like our autotuner key lost the seqlen component when cudagraph replay kicks in. cudagraphs cache the kernel selection based only on op-hash in the capture.
sara: that could explain KV cache misalignment too — if cudagraph was captured with a short prefix and then replayed on long prefix, the chosen kernel might not have tuned for the long tail, leading to spill/reschedule.
perf-bot: perf-alert: job=prod-ci-41 regression=+42% p95 compared to baseline@1876500000 [see run 41 logs] :rotating_light: 
anna: can you paste the small capture dump? curious if torch.compile inlines anything that changes op-hash.
devon: pasted snippet: 
```
# trace snippet (simplified)
op: scaled_dot_product_attention(shape=[B, H, S, S], kv_cache_offset=256)
op.hash = 0x7ef
capture.options = { cudagraphs: true, dynamic_shapes: true }
selected_kernel = kernel_table.lookup(op.hash)
selected_kernel.id = fast_kv_v2 (but tuned for seqlen bucket=32)
```
When replaying at seqlen=512 we still hit that selected_kernel because the op.hash matches capture, autotuner wasn't keyed by seqlen_range.
mike: i rolled out a change yesterday that deduplicates autotune entries by op.structural_hash only — intended to reduce table size. looks like a regression for sequence-sensitive kernels.
sara: quick mitigation: disable cudagraphs for ops flagged dynamic_shapes or when kv_cache_offset!=0. cheap to add a guard in the capture handshake.
anna: agree. also add seqlen_bucket + kv_offset flag to autotune key so we don't collide. we should also emit kernel_hash and tuner_key in per-request traces for faster triage.
mike: i'll rollback the dedupe patch on the autotuner and push a tiny guard to disable cudagraph capture for dynshape ops in canary.
devon: thanks — what about a long-term fix?
mike: long-term plan: (1) extend autotuner key to include compile-mode (torch.compile/cudagraphs), seqlen_bucket, and kv_offset; (2) make kernel selection deterministic when capture.replay==true by re-checking runtime shapes on replay and forcing a reselect when mismatch detected; (3) add an alert rule for kernel_hash reuse across kernel_group ids.
sara: + add a perf unit test that simulates capture at seqlen=32 then replay at seqlen=512 and asserts kernel.id or falls back gracefully.
perf-bot: note: creating ticket INF-2317 to track rollback + guard + autotune-key work :white_check_mark:
anna: i'll own adding trace fields and the perf unit; assigning myself. tagging @mike for rollback. please post canary link.
mike: deploying rollback to canary now, will post link in 5m.
devon: appreciate it — also let's make sure KV cache validity checks are included so we don't corrupt caches when kernel implementation changes.
anna: noted. adding to INF-2317 checklist.
devon: any objections to disabling cudagraphs for now for dynshape-heavy models across dedicated? :thumbsup: if we get majority thumbs, i'll schedule the config change.
mike: :+1: do it.
sara: +1.
perf-bot: update: canary deployed at 1876543290; perf baseline checks running.
anna: will watch. thanks all.
__notes: Single-thread Slack conversation about autotuner miskeying + cudagraph capture mismatch causing kernel reuse across seqlen buckets leading to perf regression. Names are Redwood team members, perf-bot included.
